upstream_test: code/swmf: Param/SWPC/PARAM.in_SWPC_simple_init (upstream example deck, init stage; no Makefile.test target)
configuration: Config.pl -default -v=Empty,GM/BATSRUS,IE/Ridley_serial,IM/RCM2, Config.pl -o=GM:u=Default,e=Mhd,ng=2,g=8,8,8,IE:g=181,361, then make SWMF and make PIDL. Deck PARAM.in_SWPC_simple_init from ic/, copied into a run directory made by make rundir together with IMF.dat, SATELLITES.in, sat01.dat and magin_GEM.dat: two steady-state sessions stopping at iteration 70 and iteration 200 (MaxIter is cumulative) and then a 120 s time-accurate window, which is the graded run. Run with mpiexec -n 8. Graded: log.log, magnetometers.mag, geoindex.log, ie.log, ionosphere.idl, superindex.log, mag_grid_global.out.
observable: the GM volume-average, pressure-extremum and Dst history, the thirteen ground magnetometer stations with their MHD, field-aligned, Hall and Pedersen parts, the synthetic Kp, AL, AU, AE and AO geomagnetic indices, the ionospheric cross-polar-cap potential, integrated field-aligned currents and hemispheric power, the whole two-dimensional ionosphere solution on the Ridley_serial grid (conductances, field-aligned current, potential, precipitation and the mapped inner-magnetosphere state in both hemispheres) and the synthetic SuperMAG SML, SMU, SME and SMR indices
default_vs_upstream: this deck ships without a Makefile.test target, so run.sh applies to it the same _rundir edits the Makefile.test recipe applies to the sibling SWPC decks: the MaxIter 700 and 1500 and MaxBlock 5000 reduction to 70, 200 and 350, the 360x171 and 221x131 magnetometer grids to 72x25 and 23x13, and the #BORIS line commented out. The Boris correction is the one physics switch the recipe touches, and it is not optional here: with #BORIS left active this deck goes to NaN in advance_explicit about fifteen steps into the time-accurate session (measured on 2026-09-05 at both 2 and 8 ranks, and with the #COMPONENTMAP left as shipped and swapped), while with the recipe's own disable it runs to the end of the window; the two runtime knobs SAB_STEADY_SCALE and SAB_STOP_SCALE are graded at 0.5 and 0.25, cut from the upstream's own 70/200-iteration, 120 s reduction to fit the suite inside its budget: the steady sessions now stop at iteration 35 and iteration 100, the time-accurate window is 30 s (six GM-IE couplings at the deck's 5 s DtCouple, three GM-IM/IE-IM/GM-RB couplings at 10 s); every output cadence this check grades (the magnetometer station and grid files, the geomagnetic and SuperMAG index logs, the ionosphere plot) is cut from its upstream value to a few seconds so the shorter window still carries several saved frames, which the upstream recipe does not need to do; the run uses 8 MPI ranks under the deck's own #COMPONENTMAP rather than the 2 of the Makefile.test MPIRUN default, which changes the domain decomposition; 8 was chosen by measurement, since the ionospheric potential solve is serial per hemisphere and 16 ranks are no faster than 8; the reference is produced at grading time by this same script, so the upstream stored TestOutput* files and their .gz form play no part.
variant: BodyNDim, the number density of the ionospheric inner boundary that sets both the initial state inside the body and the density fed back to the boundary every coupling, is 28 in ic/nominal and 28.0000000028 in ic/variant of PARAM.in_SWPC_simple_init - two units of the tenth significant digit, about 1e-10 relative, which is five orders of magnitude above binary64 resolution and far below any physically meaningful change of the boundary. It is generic numerical-noise calibration: the two decks differ by one number, and the spread between the two runs is the floor this pass policy can be held to.
altbuild: run.sh altbuild rebuilds the same pinned source and deck with ./Config.pl -O0 (every OPTn line of Makefile.conf forced to -O0 where the shipped gfortran template builds at -O3) before make SWMF.

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck: run.sh altbuild (the same Config.pl configuration built with ./Config.pl -O0 before make SWMF) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py

warrant: The graded observable is the GM volume-average, pressure-extremum and Dst history, the thirteen ground magnetometer stations with their MHD, field-aligned, Hall and Pedersen parts, the synthetic Kp, AL, AU, AE and AO geomagnetic indices, the ionospheric cross-polar-cap potential, integrated field-aligned currents and hemispheric power, the whole two-dimensional ionosphere solution on the Ridley_serial grid (conductances, field-aligned current, potential, precipitation and the mapped inner-magnetosphere state in both hemispheres) and the synthetic SuperMAG SML, SMU, SME and SMR indices, compared value by value under |candidate - reference| <= atol + rtol*|reference| with the per-file bounds this rubric lists. Physical: A port that gets the coupled Geospace step wrong - a magnetohydrodynamic flux or limiter that loses a term, a field-line trace that maps the inner boundary to the wrong ionospheric footpoint, an ionospheric potential solve that stops at a looser residual than the deck's 1e-6, a conductance or precipitation model that is evaluated on the wrong hemisphere, or a Biot-Savart integral with the wrong volume weight - moves these numbers by orders of magnitude more than these bounds: the volume averages of the log carry the whole domain and shift in their fourth or fifth significant digit as soon as a flux, a source term or a boundary map is wrong, the cross-polar-cap potential and the integrated field-aligned currents shift with any error in the GM-to-IE mapping, and the ionosphere file and the magnetometer output carry every point of the solution, so a fault local to the polar cap or to one refinement level shows there even where the averages hide it. The date, the grid shape and the declared number of variables are graded alongside the data, so a port that writes a different number of frames or ends on a different block tree fails on shape rather than on tolerance; the adaptive-solver iteration or call count itself (log.log's and geoindex.log's `it`, magnetometers.mag's `nstep`, mag_grid's nStep, the ionosphere file's nSolve) is bookkeeping, is not graded, and a correct port may reach the same simulated instant on a different count. Achievable: The bounds are the ones the upstream checks of the sibling SWPC test targets apply to these same output files (log.log at 1e-05 relative and 2e-08 absolute; magnetometers.mag at 0.0002 relative and 4e-05 absolute; geoindex.log at 1e-05 relative and 1e-08 absolute; ie.log at 1e-05 relative and 1e-30 absolute; ionosphere.idl at 0.0004 relative and 7e-05 absolute; superindex.log at 0.0002 relative and 0.0002 absolute; mag_grid_global.out at 0.0002 relative and 0.0002 absolute), which this deck writes in the same formats from the same code paths; they are not tightened, because the volume averages and the index sums are MPI reductions over the whole domain whose summation order is fixed only for a fixed rank count (GM/BATSRUS/src/ModWriteLogSatFile.f90, src/ModGroundMagPerturb.f90), the limiter and the conservative criterion are hard switches on cell values (src/ModFaceValue.f90, src/ModPhysics.f90) that round-off can cross, the field-line trace that builds the GM-IE mapping terminates on a search (src/ModFieldTrace.f90), and the ionospheric potential comes out of a preconditioned GMRES iteration stopped at a relative residual of 1e-6 (IE/Ridley_serial/src/ionosphere.f90), so a port that reorders its arithmetic has to be allowed to land a little away from the reference. the floor and the nominal-versus-variant spread are measured by selfcheck and recorded in evidence below.
